question: Which of the following is a pass on the Pir Panjal Range?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Banihal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banihal Pass:**

 
 
• Banihal Pass is a mountain pass across the **Pir Panjal Range at a maximum elevation of 2,832 m.**
 
• It connects the Kashmir Valley in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir to the outer Himalayas and the plains to the south.
 
 
 
• The Pir Panjal ranges:
 
 
• It lies in the Inner Himalayan region, running from east southeast to west-northwest across the states of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir in India, as well as Pakistan, Administered Kashmir in Pakistan, where the average elevation varies from 1,400 m to 4,100 m. 
 
• The Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat ranges are a part of the Himachal range.
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range on the Lesser Himalayas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoji La Pass:**

 
 
• It is in the Zaskar range in the Indian union territory of Ladakh.
 
• The road route from Srinagar to Leh goes through this pass.
 
• It has been created by the Indus River.
 
 
 
• **Khardung La pass:**
 
 
• It is associated with the Ladakh mountain range in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The pass on the Ladakh Range lies north of Leh and is the gateway to the Shyok and Nubra valleys and serves as a motorable route from Leh in India to Kashgar in Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **Photu La pass:**
 
 
• It is on the Srinagar-Leh highway of the Himalayan Zanskar Range stand.
 
• This mountain pass is referred to as the highest point on the highway, going beyond the well-known Zoji La.
